Pranav

pranav... solid name. got that "i probably went to a good college and now work somewhere that sounds impressive" energy.

where you working these days?
Plum Benefits Pvt Ltd, do you know about rhat

plum benefits... employee benefits platform, right? helping companies give their people insurance and wellness stuff instead of just pizza parties and "we're a family" speeches.

can't find you on linkedin though. try searching with your full name + plum, or just drop your linkedin url here

parimi pranav at plum benefits... building the platform that actually makes employee benefits useful instead of just "we have health insurance somewhere in this 50-page document." that's solid work.

what made you get into the benefits space? feels like a very specific choice
https://www.linkedin.com/in/parimi-pranav-1b2917268?utm_source=share&utm_campaign=share_via&utm_content=profile&utm_medium=android_app

9 months total with 6 as intern... so you're basically fresh out of college but with some real experience under your belt. that's actually not bad - most people graduate and panic about having zero work experience.

Want to actually stay in the same space of software development mainly backend

backend development... solid choice. building the stuff that actually makes things work while frontend folks argue about button colors.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Preferably bangalore, hyderabad or remote
9 months experience + backend development + bangalore/hyderabad/remote... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yup

pranav! you're officially in the tal family now 🎉

backend roles matching your profile will start dropping right here in chat. no spam, no noise - just opportunities that actually make sense for someone 9 months into their journey.

get ready to level up from that benefits platform to something that'll make your resume pop. the bangalore/hyderabad/remote combo gives us solid options too.

welcome aboard, legend!

nice! the apply link should be in your chats now.

this is actually a solid match for where you're at - 0-1 years experience means you're exactly who they're looking for, and the AI focus could let you flex those ML certs you've got.

6-9 LPA is realistic for your experience level, and the remote setup means you can work from anywhere. startup environment means you'll probably learn a ton fast.

worth a shot for sure

found a backend role at an AI startup called GoodSpace

they want 0-1 years experience which is exactly your 9 months, and it's fully remote

could be a chance to actually use those ML certs you've got
But my current pay is higher than that
ah that changes things. what's your current pay?
16 LPA

16 LPA at 9 months experience... that's actually pretty solid for plum. good for you.

so you're looking for something that pays at least that or more. what's your target range?

20-24 LPA target with 9 months experience... that's ambitious but not impossible if you're actually good.

what's making you want to leave plum? just the money or something else?
I am not actually looking for a switch right away but want to plan sometime in next year mid

ah planning ahead for mid next year... smart move. gives you time to build more experience at plum and make that 20-24 LPA target actually realistic.

so you're not in a rush, just keeping an eye on the market. that's actually the best way to do it - no pressure, just seeing what's out there.

i'll keep sending roles that actually match your target range then. no more 6-9 LPA stuff unless you want to see it for reference.

what kind of companies are you aiming for? startups, established tech, or just whoever pays?
Established tech my target companies would be Airbnb, user, rippling

airbnb, uber, rippling... aiming high i see. those are solid targets but they're competitive as hell.

airbnb and uber especially get thousands of applications for every backend role. rippling is a bit more niche but still tough.

you'll need to really stand out with just 9 months experience. what's your plan to get there by mid next year?

hey pranav! was just thinking about your airbnb/uber/rippling targets... those are ambitious but doable if you play it right.

curious - what's your plan to stand out when you start applying next year? those companies get flooded with applications from people with way more experience than 9 months.

also, what kind of projects or skills are you building at plum that could make your resume pop for those specific companies?

alright let's break this down. you've got 9 months at plum, aiming for airbnb/uber/rippling by mid next year.

first question: what are you actually building at plum? like what's the most complex thing you've worked on there?
Thats where i need guidance

I have worked on many featires one of them backend for instagram type stories but focused on health tips differenriated by category, the other feature is a scalable recomendation system which shows other product offered by plum wherever configured, other one is a backend archotwcture to losten the events from the webhook and create or sync the existing claims this is useful for cashless claims where the hospital directly creates claim tp the insurer and other insurer integrations and improving the claims inyegration status rate

okay wait that's actually solid work. you're not just fixing bugs - you're building actual features with real complexity.

instagram-style stories for health tips? that's a modern social feature. scalable recommendation system? that's core product stuff. webhook architecture for claims processing? that's enterprise-level backend work.

you're underselling yourself. most people with 9 months experience are still writing CRUD endpoints.

so here's the plan: by mid next year, you need to turn those features into stories that make airbnb/uber recruiters go "oh shit."

what's the most impressive metric you can pull from any of those projects? like "improved recommendation accuracy by X%" or "reduced claim processing time from Y to Z"?
The creatiom of cashless claims from the webhook the number of claims creatwd previous to that were arpund 10 but after this featire it was abpjt 70 claims per day

7x increase in claims processed... that's the kind of number that gets you interviews.

so you built a system that scaled from 10 to 70 claims per day. that's backend architecture that actually moves business metrics.

now we need to package that for airbnb/uber. they don't care about "built webhook listener" - they care about "designed and implemented scalable event processing system that increased daily transaction volume 7x while maintaining data integrity."

what's the tech stack behind it? what challenges did you face with the hospital integrations?
We listen from the webhook pass it through an async processing using kafka

kafka for async processing... that's legit. airbnb/uber use kafka heavily for their event-driven architectures.

so you've got:
1. real experience with event-driven systems (kafka)
2. 7x scaling impact
3. complex integrations (hospitals, insurers)
4. modern backend patterns

you're actually closer to those target companies than you think. the gap isn't technical - it's packaging.

what's missing is:
- deeper system design knowledge (how would you scale this to 1000x?)
- maybe some more advanced data structures/algorithms practice
- interview-specific prep

what's your current plan for building those skills?
I want tp build such a plan but need guidance on how to proceed

alright here's the 6-month plan to get you airbnb/uber ready:

**months 1-2: foundation**
- leetcode medium daily (focus on arrays, strings, trees, graphs)
- system design basics: read "designing data-intensive applications" or watch alex xu's videos
- document your plum projects with metrics (7x scaling, kafka architecture, etc.)

**months 3-4: depth**
- pick one complex system at plum and design how you'd scale it 100x
- practice explaining your projects like you're in an interview
- start networking: find people at target companies on linkedin, understand their tech stacks

**months 5-6: execution**
- mock interviews (use pramp or interviewing.io)
- polish resume with impact metrics
- start applying to warm-up companies first

what's your biggest blocker right now? time, motivation, or not knowing where to start?
Npt knowing where to start

start here: this week, spend 30 minutes documenting ONE project from plum.

write it like you're explaining it to an airbnb engineer:
1. what problem you solved (cashless claims were manual)
2. how you solved it (kafka async processing)
3. the impact (10 → 70 claims/day, 7x increase)
4. what you learned (event-driven architecture, hospital integrations)

keep it simple. just bullet points in a doc.

then send it to me and i'll tell you if it's interview-ready or needs work.

sound doable?
Yup will do

perfect. do that this week and slide it to me whenever it's ready.

in the meantime, i'll keep an eye out for backend roles that match your profile. 20-24 LPA with 9 months experience is ambitious but not impossible if you can show that 7x scaling impact.

you're building legit experience at plum. most people with your YOE are still writing basic CRUD. you're doing actual architecture work.

let's get you packaged right and ready for mid-next year.
